passages.text: At Iconium, Paul and Barnabas went as usual into the Jewish synagogue, where they spoke so well that a great number of Jews and Greeks believed.
passages.sermon:
Paul and Barnabas were Christian apostles.
They arrived at Iconium.
They went into the Jewish synagogue, as they usually did.
They spoke to the people there.
They spoke very effectively.
Many Jews believed their message.
Many Greeks also believed.
passages.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν Ἰκονίῳ κατὰ τὸ αὐτὸ εἰσελθεῖν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν τῶν Ἰουδαίων καὶ λαλῆσαι οὕτως ὥστε πιστεῦσαι Ἰουδαίων τε καὶ Ἑλλήνων πολὺ πλῆθος

passages.text: But the unbelieving Jews stirred up the Gentiles and poisoned their minds against the brothers.
passages.sermon:
Some Jews did not believe.
These unbelieving Jews acted against the brothers.
They stirred up the Gentiles.
They poisoned the minds of the Gentiles against the brothers.
passages.original: οἱ δὲ ἀπειθήσαντες Ἰουδαῖοι ἐπήγειραν καὶ ἐκάκωσαν τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν ἐθνῶν κατὰ τῶν ἀδελφῶν

passages.text: So Paul and Barnabas spent considerable time there, speaking boldly for the Lord, who affirmed the message of His grace by enabling them to perform signs and wonders.
passages.sermon:
Paul and Barnabas were apostles of Jesus Christ.
They stayed in Iconium for a long time.
They spoke boldly for the Lord.
The Lord confirmed the message of His grace.
He enabled Paul and Barnabas to perform signs and wonders through their hands.
passages.original: ἱκανὸν μὲν οὖν χρόνον διέτριψαν παρρησιαζόμενοι ἐπὶ τῷ Κυρίῳ τῷ μαρτυροῦντι ἐπὶ τῷ λόγῳ τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ διδόντι σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα γίνεσθαι διὰ τῶν χειρῶν αὐτῶν

passages.text: The people of the city were divided. Some sided with the Jews, and others with the apostles.
passages.sermon: The people in the city disagreed with each other.\r\nSome people supported the Jews.\r\nOther people supported the apostles.
passages.original: Ἐσχίσθη δὲ τὸ πλῆθος τῆς πόλεως καὶ οἱ μὲν ἦσαν σὺν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις οἱ δὲ σὺν τοῖς ἀποστόλοις

passages.text: But when the Gentiles and Jews, together with their rulers, set out to mistreat and stone them, they found out about it and fled to the Lycaonian cities of Lystra and Derbe and to the surrounding region, where they continued to preach the gospel.
passages.sermon:
Paul and Barnabas were apostles.
Gentiles and Jews joined together with their rulers.
They planned to mistreat Paul and Barnabas.
They also planned to stone them.
Paul and Barnabas learned about this plan.
They fled to the cities of Lystra and Derbe in Lycaonia.
They also went to the surrounding region.
In those places, Paul and Barnabas continued to preach the gospel.
passages.original: ὡς δὲ ἐγένετο ὁρμὴ τῶν ἐθνῶν τε καὶ Ἰουδαίων σὺν τοῖς ἄρχουσιν αὐτῶν ὑβρίσαι καὶ λιθοβολῆσαι αὐτούς συνιδόντες κατέφυγον εἰς τὰς πόλεις τῆς Λυκαονίας Λύστραν καὶ Δέρβην καὶ τὴν περίχωρον κἀκεῖ εὐαγγελιζόμενοι ἦσαν

passages.text: In Lystra there sat a man crippled in his feet, who was lame from birth and had never walked.
passages.sermon:
A man sat in Lystra.
He could not use his feet.
He was lame from birth.
He had never walked.
passages.original: Καί τις ἀνὴρ ἀδύνατος ἐν Λύστροις τοῖς ποσὶν ἐκάθητο χωλὸς ἐκ κοιλίας μητρὸς αὐτοῦ ὃς οὐδέποτε περιεπάτησεν

passages.text: This man was listening to the words of Paul, who looked intently at him and saw that he had faith to be healed.
passages.sermon:
A man sat in Lystra.
He could not use his feet.
He was lame from birth.
He had never walked.
Paul spoke to the people.
The lame man listened to Paul.
Paul looked closely at the man.
Paul saw that the man had faith.
Paul saw that the man believed he could be healed.
passages.original: οὗτος ἤκουσεν τοῦ Παύλου λαλοῦντος ὃς ἀτενίσας αὐτῷ καὶ ἰδὼν ὅτι ἔχει πίστιν τοῦ σωθῆναι

passages.text: In a loud voice Paul called out, “Stand up on your feet!” And the man jumped up and began to walk.
passages.sermon:
Paul spoke in a loud voice.
Paul said, “Stand up on your feet!”
The man jumped up.
The man began to walk.
passages.original: εἶπεν μεγάλῃ φωνῇ Ἀνάστηθι ἐπὶ τοὺς πόδας σου ὀρθός καὶ ἥλατο καὶ περιεπάτει

passages.text: When the crowds saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voices in the Lycaonian language: “The gods have come down to us in human form!”
passages.sermon:
Paul was an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul healed a man who had faith to be healed.
A large crowd saw what Paul did.
The crowd spoke in the Lycaonian language.
The crowd shouted loudly.
The crowd said, "The gods have come down to us in human form."
passages.original: Οἵ τε ὄχλοι ἰδόντες ὃ ἐποίησεν Παῦλος ἐπῆραν τὴν φωνὴν αὐτῶν Λυκαονιστὶ λέγοντες Οἱ θεοὶ ὁμοιωθέντες ἀνθρώποις κατέβησαν πρὸς ἡμᾶς

passages.text: Barnabas they called Zeus, and Paul they called Hermes, because he was the chief speaker.
passages.sermon:
The crowds saw what Paul had done.
They spoke in the Lycaonian language.
They called Barnabas Zeus.
They called Paul Hermes.
Paul was the chief speaker.
passages.original: ἐκάλουν τε τὸν Βαρνάβαν Δία τὸν δὲ Παῦλον Ἑρμῆν ἐπειδὴ αὐτὸς ἦν ὁ ἡγούμενος τοῦ λόγου

passages.text: The priest of Zeus, whose temple was just outside the city, brought bulls and wreaths to the city gates, hoping to offer a sacrifice along with the crowds.
passages.sermon:
The priest served Zeus.
Zeus had a temple just outside the city.
The priest brought bulls to the city gates.
He also brought wreaths to the city gates.
He came with the crowds.
He wanted to offer a sacrifice.
passages.original: ὅ τε ἱερεὺς τοῦ Διὸς τοῦ ὄντος πρὸ τῆς πόλεως ταύρους καὶ στέμματα ἐπὶ τοὺς πυλῶνας ἐνέγκας σὺν τοῖς ὄχλοις ἤθελεν θύειν

passages.text: But when the apostles Barnabas and Paul found out about this, they tore their clothes and rushed into the crowd, shouting, “Men, why are you doing this? We too are only men, human like you. We are bringing you good news that you should turn from these worthless things to the living God, who made heaven and earth and sea and everything in them.
passages.sermon:
Barnabas and Paul were apostles.
They heard what the people were doing.
They tore their clothes.
They rushed into the crowd.
They shouted loudly.
They said, “Men, why are you doing this?”
“We are only men.”
“We are human, just like you.”
“We bring you good news.”
“You should turn away from these worthless things.”
“You should turn to the living God.”
The living God made heaven.
He made earth.
He made the sea.
He made everything in them.”
passages.original: Ἀκούσαντες δὲ οἱ ἀπόστολοι Βαρνάβας καὶ Παῦλος διαρρήξαντες τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτῶν ἐξεπήδησαν εἰς τὸν ὄχλον κράζοντες καὶ λέγοντες Ἄνδρες τί ταῦτα ποιεῖτε καὶ ἡμεῖς ὁμοιοπαθεῖς ἐσμεν ὑμῖν ἄνθρωποι εὐαγγελιζόμενοι ὑμᾶς ἀπὸ τούτων τῶν ματαίων ἐπιστρέφειν ἐπὶ θεὸν ζῶντα ὃς ἐποίησεν τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτοῖς

passages.text: In past generations, He let all nations go their own way.
passages.sermon: God acted in past generations.\r\nGod allowed all nations to go their own way.\r\nEach nation followed its own path.
passages.original: ὃς ἐν ταῖς παρῳχημέναις γενεαῖς εἴασεν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη πορεύεσθαι ταῖς ὁδοῖς αὐτῶν

passages.text: Yet He has not left Himself without testimony to His goodness: He gives you rain from heaven and fruitful seasons, filling your hearts with food and gladness.”
passages.sermon:
God is the living God.
God shows His goodness to all people.
God does not leave Himself without a witness.
God gives you rain from heaven.
God gives you fruitful seasons.
God fills your hearts with food.
God fills your hearts with gladness.
passages.original: καίτοι οὐκ ἀμάρτυρον αὑτὸν ἀφῆκεν ἀγαθουργῶν οὐρανόθεν ὑμῖν ὑετοὺς διδοὺς καὶ καιροὺς καρποφόρους ἐμπιπλῶν τροφῆς καὶ εὐφροσύνης τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν

passages.text: Even with these words, Paul and Barnabas could hardly stop the crowds from sacrificing to them.
passages.sermon:
Paul and Barnabas spoke to the crowds.
They told the crowds not to sacrifice to them.
The crowds wanted to offer sacrifices to Paul and Barnabas.
Paul and Barnabas could hardly stop them.
Even after speaking, the crowds almost sacrificed to them.
passages.original: Καὶ ταῦτα λέγοντες μόλις κατέπαυσαν τοὺς ὄχλους τοῦ μὴ θύειν αὐτοῖς

passages.text: Then some Jews arrived from Antioch and Iconium and won over the crowds. They stoned Paul and dragged him outside the city, presuming he was dead.
passages.sermon:
Some Jews came from Antioch and Iconium.
These Jews persuaded the crowds.
The crowds stoned Paul.
They dragged Paul outside the city.
They thought Paul was dead.
passages.original: Ἐπῆλθαν δὲ ἀπὸ Ἀντιοχείας καὶ Ἰκονίου Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ πείσαντες τοὺς ὄχλους καὶ λιθάσαντες τὸν Παῦλον ἔσυρον ἔξω τῆς πόλεως νομίζοντες αὐτὸν τεθνηκέναι

passages.text: But after the disciples had gathered around him, he got up and went back into the city. And the next day he left with Barnabas for Derbe.
passages.sermon:
Paul was a Christian preacher.
Some people stoned Paul and dragged him outside the city.
They thought Paul was dead.
The disciples gathered around Paul.
Paul got up.
Paul went back into the city.
The next day, Paul left the city.
Barnabas went with Paul.
Paul and Barnabas traveled to Derbe.
passages.original: κυκλωσάντων δὲ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτὸν ἀναστὰς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὴν πόλιν Καὶ τῇ ἐπαύριον ἐξῆλθεν σὺν τῷ Βαρνάβᾳ εἰς Δέρβην

passages.text: They preached the gospel to that city and made many disciples. Then they returned to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch, strengthening the souls of the disciples and encouraging them to continue in the faith. “We must endure many hardships to enter the kingdom of God,” they said.
passages.sermon:
Paul and Barnabas preached the gospel in that city.
They made many disciples there.
They returned to Lystra.
They returned to Iconium.
They returned to Antioch.
They strengthened the souls of the disciples in those places.
They encouraged the disciples to continue in the faith.
They said, “We must endure many hardships to enter the kingdom of God.”
passages.original: Εὐαγγελισάμενοί τε τὴν πόλιν ἐκείνην καὶ μαθητεύσαντες ἱκανοὺς ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς τὴν Λύστραν καὶ εἰς Ἰκόνιον καὶ εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν ἐπιστηρίζοντες τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν μαθητῶν παρακαλοῦντες ἐμμένειν τῇ πίστει καὶ ὅτι Διὰ πολλῶν θλίψεων δεῖ ἡμᾶς εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: Paul and Barnabas appointed elders for them in each church, praying and fasting as they entrusted them to the Lord, in whom they had believed.
passages.sermon:
Paul and Barnabas traveled together.
They visited each church.
They chose elders for each church.
They prayed for the elders.
They fasted while they prayed.
They entrusted the elders to the Lord.
The believers in these churches trusted in the Lord.
passages.original: Χειροτονήσαντες δὲ αὐτοῖς κατ’ ἐκκλησίαν πρεσβυτέρους προσευξάμενοι μετὰ νηστειῶν παρέθεντο αὐτοὺς τῷ Κυρίῳ εἰς ὃν πεπιστεύκεισαν

passages.text: After passing through Pisidia, they came to Pamphylia.
passages.sermon: Paul and Barnabas traveled through Pisidia.\r\nThey arrived in Pamphylia.
passages.original: Καὶ διελθόντες τὴν Πισιδίαν ἦλθον εἰς τὴν Παμφυλίαν

passages.text: And when they had spoken the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia.
passages.sermon: Paul and Barnabas spoke the word of God in Perga.\r\nThey went down to Attalia.
passages.original: καὶ λαλήσαντες ἐν Πέργῃ τὸν λόγον κατέβησαν εἰς Ἀττάλειαν

passages.text: From Attalia they sailed to Antioch, where they had been commended to the grace of God for the work they had just completed.
passages.sermon:
Paul and his companions left Attalia.
They sailed to Antioch.
The church in Antioch had sent them out.
The church had entrusted them to the grace of God.
God’s grace helped them do their work.
They finished the work God gave them.
passages.original: Κἀκεῖθεν ἀπέπλευσαν εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν ὅθεν ἦσαν παραδεδομένοι τῇ χάριτι τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰς τὸ ἔργον ὃ ἐπλήρωσαν

passages.text: When they arrived, they gathered the church together and reported all that God had done through them, and how He had opened the door of faith to the Gentiles.
passages.sermon:
Paul and Barnabas arrived in Antioch.
They gathered the church together.
They spoke to the believers.
They reported everything God had done through them.
God had worked with Paul and Barnabas.
God had opened the door of faith to the Gentiles.
The Gentiles could now believe in Jesus Christ.
passages.original: Παραγενόμενοι δὲ καὶ συναγαγόντες τὴν ἐκκλησίαν ἀνήγγελλον ὅσα ἐποίησεν ὁ Θεὸς μετ’ αὐτῶν καὶ ὅτι ἤνοιξεν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν θύραν πίστεως

passages.text: And they spent a long time there with the disciples.
passages.sermon:
Paul and Barnabas were apostles and missionaries.
\r\nThey stayed in Antioch.
\r\nThey remained there for a long time.
\r\nThey spent this time with the disciples.
passages.original: διέτριβον δὲ χρόνον οὐκ ὀλίγον σὺν τοῖς μαθηταῖς
